sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:1
items.html:
To understand the words of the ARI from here on, you must review here the explanation of the five discernments in the screen, which emerge by force of the refinement of the screen, in order of degree, from the great coarseness of phase four to the great refinement in the discernment of Keter and the root of the screen, by which they make five Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf]. You will find these matters explained in Part 2 (in Inner Observation, the passage beginning “And know.” Review there the entire continuation up to the passage beginning “And the world of Assiya,” and after that, the passage beginning “And by what has been explained,” and review the entire continuation up to the passage beginning “However”). For all these matters belong here, but it is impossible to bring them because of their length; therefore I must rely on what I have already explained there, and I can bring here only a summary and the conclusion of each matter, to the extent needed for the words of the ARI here.
And it was explained there that the light of Ein Sof, which includes the four phases called the ten Sefirot of direct light, does not cease shining to the lower ones even for a moment. But since there is no grasp at all of light without a vessel, therefore only a vessel of reception is needed. And every Partzuf and degree, at the very moment it attains a vessel, immediately attains the light along with it, to the measure of the vessel it has attained. It was also explained there that the root of all the vessels in all the worlds is the reflected light that rises from the coupling by striking on the screen in the vessel of Malchut. Thus, the very moment a new screen comes into being in some Partzuf, the light of Ein Sof, which includes the ten Sefirot of direct light, immediately expands to it and strikes on this screen, and reflected light rises and clothes the light of Ein Sof according to the measure of the size of that reflected light. And this is what is called the clothing of Ein Sof in the vessels, or in some Sefira. For the name of a Sefira indicates the measure of the level of the light of Ein Sof that is clothed there. For example, when we say the clothing of Ein Sof in Keter, it indicates that the reflected light clothes all ten Sefirot of direct light, up to Keter; and when we say the clothing of Ein Sof in Hochma, it indicates that the reflected light clothes only up to Hochma. And one should not ask: if so, there are only nine Sefirot in this clothing, whereas we hold “ten and not nine.” For in truth there is also Keter there, but this Keter is clothed in the internality of Hochma, and therefore it does not appear in the name, but only the Sefira of Hochma alone. And in this way you will understand all the levels of the other Partzufim.
It was also explained there what the yardstick is by which the size of each reflected light is measured: it is the discernment of the measure of coarseness included in the screen in the vessel of Malchut, and these are five discernments. For the coarsest screen, which is phase four — the measure of the reflected light returned from it is the greatest, and it is the one that clothes up to the level of Keter in the light of Ein Sof, that is, of the ten Sefirot of direct light. A screen whose coarseness is phase three clothes at the level of Hochma of the ten Sefirot of direct light. A screen whose coarseness is only phase two clothes at the level of Bina of the ten Sefirot of direct light. A screen whose coarseness is only phase one clothes only up to the level of ZA of the ten Sefirot of direct light. And a screen that has no coarseness, but only the discernment of the root of the screen, called the Keter of the screen — in this screen no coupling by striking applies at all, and it has no measure of level whatsoever, but only according to the measure of the Sefira of Malchut alone. However, one must remember all the reasons and grounds of these matters, as they were explained there in the above-mentioned Inner Observation and in the previous parts; study it there well. For without understanding the reasons and necessities in these matters, it is impossible to understand even a single word here thoroughly, since here I am compelled to be brief, as is understood.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:2
items.html:
Explanation: The world of Atzilut is regarded as the Rosh [head] of all the worlds. And although there are many worlds above Atzilut, namely all the numerous worlds included in the world of Adam Kadmon, they are nevertheless all concealed within the world of Atzilut, and they are not a root for the worlds at all; rather, they are regarded as a root for the world of Atzilut alone, which is why they are concealed within it and shine only in it, in concealment.
And it was explained in the previous parts that the screen of phase four serves only in the world of AK alone; therefore the measure of the reflected light there is very great, and it clothes up to the level of Keter in the light of Ein Sof. Hence all the worlds included in the world of Adam Kadmon are called by the name the world of Keter.
However, in the world of Atzilut, where only the screen of phase three serves (see Inner Observation, Part 2, Chapter 2, item 10, the passage beginning “And the screen”), the measure of the reflected light that rises from the coupling by striking on that screen reaches only up to the level of Hochma, and it does not attain the Keter of the light of Ein Sof; rather, the Keter is concealed and hidden within Hochma, as above. Therefore the world of Atzilut is called by the name the world of Hochma. And this is the secret of the verse, “You have made them all in wisdom”: that is, everything is rooted in Atzilut alone, and not in the world of AK, which is the world of Keter. For the world of AK is not regarded at all as a root for the lower worlds, and nothing of it will appear in the worlds until after the end of correction, in the secret of the verse, “And his feet shall stand upon the Mount of Olives.” And one should know that just as a level of ten Sefirot is regarded entirely according to the highest Sefira in it — if it is Keter, all the Sefirot will be the discernment of Keter, and if it is Hochma, they will all be Hochma, etc. — so each world is regarded entirely according to its first Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:3
items.html: This has already been explained in the adjacent item. But it does not mean that immediately, when the world of Atzilut was emanated, it received the level of Hochma, for small levels, called Ibur [impregnation] and nursing, were emanated there first. Rather, the intention is the greatest level that finally emerged there, in AA, which is only the level of Hochma and lacks Keter.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:4
items.html: It has already been explained above that all the endlessly numerous worlds that exist before Atzilut are all included in the name Adam Kadmon, or the world of Keter. And this is for the above reason.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:5
items.html:
You already know the matter of the diminution of the reflected light, which comes because of the refinement of the measure of coarseness in the screen (see Inner Observation, Part 2, Chapter 7, item 72, the passage beginning “And in order”). Accordingly, you will understand that after the world of AK was completed, through the clothing in the reflected light of its screen of phase four, this screen was then refined to phase three, for the reason mentioned above in Inner Observation. This does not mean that any change was made in the screen of phase four in the world of AK itself, for there is no absence in spirituality; rather, every change means an addition. For through its refinement to phase three, a new screen of phase three was added, born, and emerged, to which the upper light immediately expands (as above, Chapter 3, item 1) for a coupling by striking, and it raises reflected light from the screen upward, up to the level of Hochma; and this is called a new clothing in the world of AK, namely the clothing of the light of Ein Sof in Hochma. However, this new clothing is not needed for its own sake, but only for the sake of the world of Atzilut. For because of the above-mentioned screen of phase three, whose reflected light rose from the place of the screen upward and clothed the light of Ein Sof up to the level of Hochma, all the ten Sefirot above the screen return and descend as well from the place of the screen downward, as written above (Chapter 2, item 3), where it is regarded that the screen and Malchut widen from her downward into ten Sefirot because of the reflected light that returns and is drawn to it from above. Therefore Malchut expands into ten Sefirot from her and within her, like the ten Sefirot of reflected light that rose from the screen of phase three above, that is, at the level of Hochma; and these are what are called the ten Sefirot of Atzilut.
And this is what the ARI says: “And in that Hochma that is above Atzilut, there, within it, Ein Sof clothes and shines in Atzilut.” He means to say that this coupling by striking on the screen of phase three had to be in the world of AK, which is above Atzilut, for the screen of phase three is but a refinement of phase four, and phase four is in the world of AK, as above. If so, the refinement and the coupling by striking must necessarily be in the world of AK, which is above Atzilut. And after Ein Sof clothed there, in the reflected light that rose from the screen upward, then the ten Sefirot of the world of Atzilut descended and were drawn from the place of the screen downward, as explained.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:6
items.html: Here too, as in Atzilut, it does not mean that the level of Bina emerged in the world of Beria immediately at its beginning. Rather, he means to say that the greatest level that finally emerged there is no more than the level of Bina, and the coupling was above, in phase two in Atzilut. That is, this too is for the reason explained above in the adjacent item, study it there well: the refinement of the screen from phase three to phase two, which is called Bina, must take place in the world of Atzilut, for that is the place of the screen of phase three, which is called Hochma. And just as in the four Partzufim [pl. of Partzuf] AB, SAG, MA and BON of AK the coupling of each Partzuf was made in the Peh [mouth] of the Rosh [head] of the Partzuf above it — for the coupling of AB, which is phase three, was made in the Peh of the Rosh of Partzuf Galgalta, and the coupling of SAG was made in the Peh of the Rosh of AB (as written well here in Inner Observation, Chapter 9; see there), etc. — in this way, so in the worlds of ABYA, the coupling for the sake of each world was made in the world above it. And after the screen of phase three was refined there to phase two, it is regarded that a new screen of phase two was added and born there, and the light of Ein Sof immediately expands to it for a coupling by striking, as above; and the reflected light rises and clothes up to the level of Bina of the ten Sefirot of direct light, and the Keter and Hochma of direct light clothe in the internality of Bina, as above. And after the clothing of Ein Sof in Bina from the screen upward has been completed, as said, the reflected light then returns and descends from the place of the screen downward, and widens that Malchut into ten Sefirot from her and within her, that is, from her Keter to her Malchut, like the ten Sefirot that are from the screen upward in Atzilut, that is, only at the level of Bina, in which Keter and Hochma are concealed, as above. And these ten Sefirot are the ten Sefirot of the world of Beria. Thus, the ten Sefirot at the level of Bina that emerged above the screen are in the world of Atzilut, and about them the ARI says, “When he wished to shine in Beria, he clothed in the Bina that is in Atzilut.” And the second ten Sefirot, which were drawn and emerged below the screen, are called the ten Sefirot in the world of Beria.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:7
items.html: That is, everything that is found in the ten Sefirot of the world of Beria is drawn through the ten Sefirot of the level of Bina that is above Beria, for the reason explained in the adjacent item (and see above, Chapter 2, item 3).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:3:8
items.html: That is, this too is for the reason explained above concerning Atzilut and Beria: the world of Yetzira is drawn from the screen of phase one, and the refinement from phase two to phase one must take place in the world of Beria, for that is where that screen is. And after the refinement has taken place there, ten Sefirot emerge there from the screen upward at the level of ZA, which is called Tifferet, and the first three Sefirot — Keter, Hochma, Bina of direct light — are concealed and clothed in the internality of Tifferet. And after this clothing has been completed, a second ten Sefirot return and descend from the place of the screen downward at the level of ZA, and these are called the ten Sefirot of the world of Yetzira.
